findings.reason: A concrete unit-disk picture materially clarifies the distinction between two feasible boundary steps with different directions and predicted reductions. The original standalone screenshot and identical frozen/current pre-edit carrier have no figure. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope.
findings.action: Added one native TikZ figure in final Remarks with the unit circle, coordinate axes, two step radii, solid boundary points, exact coordinate labels and predicted reductions.

correction: Appended final Remarks and a unit-circle illustration of the already computed exact minimizer and Cauchy step; original title, frontmatter, statement, Facts and proof remain byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Feasible set in R^2, boundary circle, p_* and p_C.
diagram_math_checks.check: The example fixes Delta=1 and F1 gives ||p||_2<=1. Equal x/y drawing scale and circle radius 1 depict this disk boundary without distortion. The circle is actually closed in the compiled SVG and standalone image.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Two boundary endpoints and their radial directions.
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 1.1 defines p_*=(1,1)/sqrt(2), whose squared norm is 1; step 2.1 defines p_C=(1,3)/sqrt(10), also with squared norm 1. Drawing coordinates (0.707107,0.707107) and (0.316228,0.948683) are rendering approximations to those exact labels. Distinct slopes 1 and 3 correctly separate the directions; -g=(1,3)/sqrt(2) is a positive multiple of p_C by the Example and F3.

The local model definition gives pred(p)=m(0)-m(p)=-g^T p-(p^T B p)/2. At p_*, g^T p_*=-2 and p_*^T B p_*=0, giving 2. At p_C, g^T p_C=-sqrt(5) and p_C^T B p_C=4/5, giving sqrt(5)-2/5, exactly step 2.1. No contours or additional minimization claims are introduced.

The existing two proof steps and their supplier interfaces are unchanged; Remarks explicitly states the rigorous proof is independent of the picture. Axes and arrows are geometric vectors, not morphisms or commutativity assertions.
